key_insight: CEENs improves long-time PDE solving by explicitly enforcing temporal causality during training, avoiding the late-time bias that can make standard PINNs fail.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more accurate and efficient neural solver for time-dependent PDEs, with potential value in simulation workflows that need stable long-horizon predictions.
method: Split the time domain into nonoverlapping subintervals.
Assign one neural network to each subinterval and train them sequentially from the initial time.
Use an integral-form PDE loss on each subinterval to encode causality.
Provide a parallelization scheme to speed up training and inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant accuracy gains on multiple long-time PDE problems where PINNs fail, along with lower computational cost and memory use.
watch_item: Sequential subinterval training and network chaining may increase implementation complexity and require careful tuning to keep errors from propagating across time blocks.
paper_title: CEENs: Causality-enforced evolutional networks for solving time-dependent partial differential equations
